key_insight: The paper shows that phase-pure bulk Cs2AgBiI6, a long-predicted but elusive lead-free iodide double perovskite, can be synthesized in both microcrystal and thin-film form by carefully controlling moisture during halide exchange.
engineering_relevance: This establishes a new non-toxic absorber candidate for perovskite solar and optoelectronic devices, with demonstrated stability and measurable photoconductive response.
method: Prepare phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 microcrystals as the bromide precursor
Remove trace moisture to enable complete anion exchange from Br to I
Form films by flash thermal evaporation of Cs2AgBiBr6 followed by anion exchange
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV optical bandgap, near-infrared photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, months-long room-temperature stability, and photoconductivity in phase-pure films.
watch_item: The material is still an early-stage absorber with no device-level solar-cell efficiency shown, so synthesis reproducibility and film quality will be key implementation risks.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
